name: Hephzibah
title: Mother of King Manasseh and Queen of Judah
summary: Hephzibah was the wife of King Hezekiah of Judah and the mother of King Manasseh. She is mentioned in 2 Kings as the mother of Manasseh. Her name means 'My delight is in her' and is also used symbolically by the prophet Isaiah to refer to the restored Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as the mother of Manasseh
keyEvents.description: Hephzibah is mentioned as the mother of King Manasseh when he became king over Judah at twelve years old. She was the wife of the godly King Hezekiah.

keyEvents.title: Hezekiah's marriage and heir
keyEvents.description: Hezekiah had his life extended by fifteen years after his illness, and it is likely that Manasseh was born during this period, making Hephzibah central to the continuation of the dynasty.

keyEvents.title: Manasseh's wicked reign
keyEvents.description: Hephzibah's son Manasseh became one of Judah's most ungodly kings, reinstating idolatry and shedding innocent blood in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's symbolic use of the name Hephzibah
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah uses the name 'Hephzibah' (My delight is in her) as a symbolic name for the restored Jerusalem, as a sign of God's renewed love for his people.

keyEvents.title: Part of Judah's royal dynasty
keyEvents.description: Hephzibah is part of the Davidic lineage that leads to the Messiah. Her son Manasseh is mentioned in Jesus' genealogy in the Gospel of Matthew.
